flaws.locator: Theorem 2.2, proof via Propositions 2.5 (the JPP for F) and 2.6: Proposition 2.5's step 'Without loss of generality, s^A and s^B are antidiagonals' (Lemma 2.12) and Lemma 2.13's 'other direction' (every surjective connected s^A lies in F, lifted through an antidiagonal (B, s^B) from Lemma 2.12): the lemma is applied to relations that need not be symmetric, while the epimorphic image of an antidiagonal is symmetric; v2 adds 'symmetric' to Lemmas 2.12 and 2.13 and lifts through the new Proposition lifttoinv to an involution
